simple.meaning: בָּרֹד (bârôd) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “spotted (as if with hail).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 31:10. The surrounding context includes family line, flock.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּרֹד (H1261) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: בָּרֹד (bârôd) / H1261 is traced through Genesis 31:10, Genesis 31:12, Zechariah 6:3, Zechariah 6:6 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H1261. barod [ בָּרֹד ] adjective spotted, marked (as if sprinkled with hail ? so Ki compare Lag BN 29 ; Syriac , i.e. grandinatus, grêlé , PS), masculine plural of sheep & goats וּבְרֻדִּים נְקֻדִּים עֲקֻדִּים Gen 31:10 , 12 ; horses Zech 6:3 , 6 .

occurrences.englishText: During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats which leaped on the flock were streaked, speckled, and grizzled.
He said, ‘Now lift up your eyes, and behold, all the male goats which leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.
in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot dappled horses, all of them powerful.
The one with the black horses goes out toward the north country; and the white went out after them; and the dappled went out toward the south country.”
